\newlength{\W}\setlength{\W}{79.5cm}      % Usable width.

\tcbset{enhanced, boxsep=0pt, before skip=0pt, after skip=0pt}

% Section: dark rounded frame with a tab label on the top left.
\newtcolorbox{sectionbox}[2][]{enhanced, colback=white, colframe=luceframe, boxrule=1.4mm, arc=8mm,
  left=6mm, right=6mm, top=9mm, bottom=3mm,
  attach boxed title to top left={xshift=10mm, yshift=-\tcboxedtitleheight/2},
  boxed title style={colback=luceframe, colframe=luceframe, arc=3mm, boxrule=0pt,
    left=7mm, right=7mm, top=3mm, bottom=3mm},
  title={\ftab\bfseries #2}, coltitle=white, #1}

% Panel inside a section.
\newtcolorbox{panel}[1][]{enhanced, colback=lucepanelfill, colframe=luceframe, boxrule=0.7mm, arc=5mm,
  left=4mm, right=4mm, top=3mm, bottom=3mm, #1}

% Key message of a result, under the graph, with an arrow pointing up to it.
\newtcolorbox{keybox}[1][]{enhanced, colback=lucekeyfill, colframe=luceframe, boxrule=0.9mm, arc=3mm,
  left=4mm, right=4mm, top=3mm, bottom=3mm, fontupper=\fkey\bfseries\raggedright, valign=center,
  overlay={\path[fill=luceframe] (frame.north) ++(-9mm,0) -- ++(18mm,0) -- ++(-9mm,8mm) -- cycle;}, #1}

% Placeholder: dashed grey box with an explicit label.
\newtcolorbox{placeholder}[1][]{enhanced, colback=luceplaceholder!15, colframe=luceplaceholder, boxrule=0.8mm,
  arc=2mm, borderline={0.8mm}{0mm}{white,dashed}, left=3mm, right=3mm, top=3mm, bottom=3mm,
  halign=center, valign=center, fontupper=\fcap\bfseries\color{luceplaceholder!60!black}, #1}

\newcommand{\resulttitle}[1]{{\fontsize{29}{34}\selectfont\wsp\bfseries\color{luceframe}#1\par}\vspace{2mm}}
% Caption of a result: one italic line, same height in every panel.
\newcommand{\rescaption}[1]{\par\vspace{2mm}\begin{minipage}[t][1.3cm][t]{\linewidth}\centering\fcap\itshape #1\end{minipage}\par}
% Legend of the scattering orders, shared by the two graphs of the orders panel.
% Same size (LEGEND_PT = 28) and dashes (matplotlib "--" at ORDER_LINE_PT = 1.8 pt) as the graphs.
\newcommand{\flegend}{\fontsize{28}{34}\selectfont\wsp}
\newcommand{\legline}[2]{\tikz[baseline=-0.6ex]\draw[#1, line width=1.8pt, dash pattern=on 6.7pt off 2.9pt] (0,0) -- (1.38,0);\hspace{3mm}#2}
\newcommand{\orderlegend}{{\flegend\legline{luceorder1}{Order 1}\hspace{9mm}\legline{luceorder2}{Order 2}\hspace{9mm}%
  \legline{luceorder3}{Order 3}\hspace{9mm}\legline{luceorder4}{Orders $\geq$ 4}}}
% Title of a take-home message in the Conclusions.
\newcommand{\conctitle}[1]{{\fpanel\bfseries\color{luceframe}#1\par}\vspace{2mm}\raggedright}
% Arrow from a limitation to its next step (same style as the flow arrows).
\newcommand{\conchead}[1]{{\fontsize{31}{33}\selectfont\wsp\bfseries\color{luceframe}#1}}
\newcommand{\limarrow}{\tikz[baseline=-0.6ex]\draw[line width=3pt, luceframe!45, -{Stealth[length=10pt,width=11pt]}] (0,0) -- (1.8,0);}
% Small drawings without labels (icons).
\newcommand{\nolabels}{\tikzset{lab/.style={text opacity=0, font=\fontsize{1}{1}\selectfont, inner sep=0pt}}}
% Display formula with tight spacing.
\newcommand{\eq}[1]{\par\vspace{1.6mm}{\centering\fmath$\displaystyle #1$\par}\vspace{1.6mm}}

\par\vspace{\secgap}
% ===========================================================================
% BACKGROUND | AIMS + WORKING HYPOTHESIS
% ===========================================================================
\begin{sectionbox}{Background and aims}
  \vspace{5mm}
  \begin{minipage}[c]{25.0cm}\raggedright
    LUCE (ASI--NASA) is the first three-wavelength Raman lidar mission. From 450 km, 12° off nadir, it will observe atmospheric particles, the sea surface and the upper ocean, with a channel dedicated to chlorophyll fluorescence to follow the seasonal and interannual dynamics of phytoplankton.
  \end{minipage}\hfill
  \begin{minipage}[c]{51.6cm}\raggedright
    {\fkey{\color{luceframe}\bfseries Objective:} contribute to the development of the forward model of the end-to-end mission simulator.\par}
    \par\vspace{3mm}
    {\centering\picEtoE\par}
  \end{minipage}
  \par\vspace{9mm}
  {\fkey\raggedright\setlength{\baselineskip}{41pt}%
    {\color{luceframe}\bfseries Working hypothesis:} a \textbf{semi-analytic Monte Carlo} model~[3] that treats together the \hchip{lucestep4}{slant-view geometry}, a \hchip{lucestep1}{Gaussian beam}, a \hchip{lucestep2}{wind-roughened sea surface} and \hchip{lucestep3}{multiple scattering} in water can simulate the \hchip{lucetime}{time-based profile} that a LUCE-like lidar records from the sea and can retrieve the \hchip{lucereal}{real depth profile}, including the \hchip{lucestep5}{surface glint}.\par}
\end{sectionbox}
\par\vspace{\secgap}
% ===========================================================================
% METHODS
% ===========================================================================
\begin{sectionbox}{Methods}
  % Cells of the photon cycle (left) and the big drawing of the model (right).
  \begin{minipage}[c]{36.4cm}\methodscells\end{minipage}\hfill
  \begin{minipage}[c]{40.6cm}\centering\picModel\end{minipage}
\end{sectionbox}
\par\vspace{\secgap}
% ===========================================================================
% RESULTS
% ===========================================================================
\begin{sectionbox}{Results}
  \vspace{5mm}
  % ---- R1: validation -------------------------------------------------------
  \begin{minipage}[t]{\figwcm cm}\centering
    \resulttitle{Validation against ICESat-2}
    \includegraphics[width=\figwcm cm]{figures/fig_icesat.pdf}
    \rescaption{ICESat-2 case of [4], flat sea.}
    \vspace{8mm}
    % source: runs/2026-11-17_icesat2_c0138/README.md (code v1.0-aisam2026), 60 dB fits
    % (K_t 0.0722 against 0.0719 m^-1, i.e. 0.4%; K_z 0.1049 against 0.1051 m^-1, i.e. 0.2%)
    \begin{keybox}[equal height group=reskey]Decay rates $K_z$ (real depth) and $K_t$ (time-based) within 0.5\% of the published values.\end{keybox}
  \end{minipage}\hfill
  % ---- R2: recorded versus true profile, by scattering order -----------------
  \begin{minipage}[t]{\dimexpr2\dimexpr\figwcm cm\relax+6mm\relax}\centering
    \resulttitle{What the lidar records is not the true profile}
    \includegraphics[width=\figwcm cm]{figures/fig_orders_z.pdf}\hfill
    \includegraphics[width=\figwcm cm]{figures/fig_orders_t.pdf}
    \rescaption{{\upshape\orderlegend}\unskip\hspace{12mm}LUCE-like case.}
    \vspace{8mm}
    % source: runs/2026-11-17_luce_orders/README.md (code v1.0-aisam2026): fit 5-60 m, K_z 0.1076, K_t 0.0519, ratio 2.07;
    % first bin (0-1 m), share of order 1: real 0.326, time-based 0.869 (also printed by plot/fig_orders.py)
    \begin{keybox}[equal height group=reskey]Multiply scattered photons arrive late and are recorded too deep: read as depth, the record decays half as fast as the true profile ($K_z/K_t$ = 2.07).\end{keybox}
  \end{minipage}\hfill
  % ---- R3: glint ---------------------------------------------------------------
  \begin{minipage}[t]{\figwcm cm}\centering
    \resulttitle{Glint against wind speed}
    % source: runs/2026-11-16_glint_sweep (code v1.0-aisam2026, 10^6 photons per run); plot/fig_glint.py
    \includegraphics[width=\figwcm cm]{figures/fig_glint_u10.pdf}
    \rescaption{Surface bin, one curve per off-nadir angle.}
    \vspace{8mm}
    % source: runs/2026-11-16_glint_sweep/README.md: at 0 deg the glint falls monotonically with U10
    % (x27 from 0 to 15 m/s); at 20 and 30 deg it grows monotonically; at 12 deg it grows up to 7.5-10 m/s.
    \begin{keybox}[equal height group=reskey]Near nadir the glint fades with wind; off nadir it grows, as the wind supplies facets of the required slope.\end{keybox}
  \end{minipage}
\end{sectionbox}
\par\vspace{\secgap}
% ===========================================================================
% CONCLUSIONS
% ===========================================================================
\begin{sectionbox}{Conclusions}
  \vspace{4mm}
  % ---- Three take-home messages ----------------------------------------------
  \begin{minipage}[t]{25.2cm}
  \begin{panel}[equal height group=concl]
    \conctitle{Validated}
    % source: runs/2026-11-17_icesat2_c0138/README.md (code v1.0-aisam2026), 60 dB fits
    The semi-analytic Monte Carlo model reproduces a published ICESat-2 case: both profiles decay within 0.5\% of the published rates.
  \end{panel}
  \end{minipage}\hfill
  \begin{minipage}[t]{25.2cm}
  \begin{panel}[equal height group=concl]
    \conctitle{From record to depth}
    The model links what LUCE records in time to the true depth distribution of the signal: the basis for retrieving, from the measurement, what happens in the ocean.
  \end{panel}
  \end{minipage}\hfill
  \begin{minipage}[t]{25.2cm}
  \begin{panel}[equal height group=concl]
    \conctitle{Glint}
    % source: runs/2026-11-16_glint_sweep/README.md: at 12 deg, 5.49e-19 at U10 = 0 and 4.641e-14 at
    % U10 = 7.5 m/s; at nadir, 1.293e-13 at 7.5 m/s (ratio 2.8).
    Glint is an unwanted return: at $\alpha$ = 12° it vanishes on a calm sea, but with wind it rises to within a factor of $\sim$3 of the nadir glint.
  \end{panel}
  \end{minipage}
  \par\vspace{4mm}
  % ---- Each limitation next to its next step, in one panel --------------------
  \begin{panel}
    \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}%
    \centering
    % Block centred on the page, columns flush left.
    \begin{tabular}[t]{@{}l@{\hspace{8mm}}c@{\hspace{8mm}}l@{}}
      \conchead{Limitations} & & \conchead{Next steps}\\
      Vertically homogeneous water & \limarrow & Stratified water column\\
      Henyey--Greenstein phase function & \limarrow & Measured phase functions, e.g.\ Petzold\\
      Sea surface described by slope statistics & \limarrow & Instantaneous sea surface from a Fourier decomposition of the waves\\
      Limited range of geophysical scenarios that can be simulated & \limarrow & Coupling with SCIATRAN [5]\\
    \end{tabular}
  \end{panel}
\end{sectionbox}
